title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics, tool schema mapping, and tool message formatting for function calling
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: Our OpenAI compatibility layer currently supports basic function/tool calling (name + args JSON) but diverges from recent OpenAI semantics around explicit tool_choice responses, tool message formatting (role/tool vs assistant/tool), and schema mapping for rich tool definitions. This causes downstream SDKs and customers relying on OpenAI-compatible behavior to need custom shims.

What this PR does: implements tool_choice semantics, improves mapping between Redwood tool schemas and OpenAI-style 'tools' definitions, and standardizes the formatting of tool messages in the compatibility layer. Key changes are in the compatibility runtime (runtime/openai_compat), SDK adapters, and docs.

Design notes: - tool_choice: we now map Redwood's routed-tool selection and multi-tool responses into an explicit top-level `tool_choice` object for OpenAI consumers (name, confidence, metadata) when model emits tool-selection tokens. This preserves our internal routing metadata while remaining compatible with OpenAI clients. - schema mapping: richer tool parameter schemas (objects, enums, nested props) are translated into OpenAI 'parameters' JSON Schema subset; unsupported features (oneOf/anyOf with discriminators) are downgraded with a best-effort description and a compatibility warning in the tool definition. - message formatting: tool-invocation messages were inconsistent (sometimes assistant role with tool name in text). We standardize to produce: {role: "tool", name: <tool_name>, content: <serialized payload>} for outbound tool messages in the OpenAI compatibility layer. SDK adapters are updated to accept both legacy and new formats.

Backwards compatibility: - Default behavior is backward compatible: if a downstream client expects old formatting, the SDK adapter exposes a compatibility flag `openai_compat_mode: legacy` to preserve prior output. - Feature flag `openai_compat_tool_choice` controls whether the explicit tool_choice field is emitted. We'll enable it by default after a 2-week canary.

Testing & validation: unit tests added for schema translation, e2e integration tests against the python SDK compatibility harness, and local compatibility smoke tests using a stub model that emits tool-choice tokens.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement tool_choice mapping in openai_compat runtime
- [x] Serialize tool messages with explicit role/name/content structure
- [x] Add schema translation utilities and compatibility warnings
- [x] Update Python and TypeScript SDK adapters to accept new format
- [x] Add unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs: add compatibility notes and examples in openai/func-calling.md

Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag; staged canary to 10% traffic for 3 days, monitor compatibility errors and SDK telemetry, then promote to 100% and remove legacy flag after 2 weeks.

Related: ENG-5721, ENG-5729.

review_comments: Evelyn Zhao: Can you expand on how we handle oneOf/anyOf? The current mapper drops discriminators in some cases.
Maya Patel: We downgrade oneOf/anyOf into a flat union description and emit a compatibility warning in the tool metadata. Added explicit tests demonstrating the downgrade behavior.
Luca Romano: Are there any perf implications for schema translation at request time?
Maya Patel: Schema translation runs at tool registration time and is cached; runtime path only serializes already-translated params. No measurable latency impact in perf bench.
Priya Singh: Please add a migration note about the tool message role change so downstream consumers don't break.
Maya Patel: Added migration section in openai/func-calling.md and SDK adapter flags for legacy mode.
release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: add explicit tool_choice semantics, improved tool parameter schema mapping, and standardized tool message formatting. Backwards-compatible via legacy flag; staged rollout behind feature flag.
